verses.1: Better is a loaf of bread with peace in it than a house full of feasts and strife.
verses.2: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son, and an inheritance will be shared among brothers.
verses.3: Like a refiner’s furnace for silver and a launderer’s soap for gold, the LORD examines hearts.
verses.4: An evil ear listens to the plotting tongue, and a liar’s words are honeyed on the lips of the wicked.
verses.5: Mocking the poor is an offense to the one who made him, and one who rejoices over misfortune will not go unpunished.
verses.6: The glory of the aged is their grandchildren, and the pride of parents is their children.
verses.7: It is not fitting for a fool to speak with integrity, nor for a noble to speak falsely.
verses.8: A bribe is a charm to the one giving it, and wherever it turns, it brings success.
verses.9: One who covers up faults seeks love, but one who repeats a matter separates close friends.
verses.10: A reproof strikes a wise person more than a hundred blows strike a fool.
verses.11: A rebellious man plots evil, and a cruel messenger is sent on his behalf.
verses.12: Meeting a bear with claws is better than meeting a fool in his folly.
verses.13: One who repays evil for good will never escape trouble from his own house.
verses.14: The starting point of a dispute is like a leak of water, and before a quarrel is revealed, matters are abandoned.
verses.15: Justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous are both an abomination to the LORD.
verses.16: Why would a fool have money in his hand to buy wisdom, when he has no heart for it?
verses.17: A friend is loyal in every time, and a brother is born for times of trouble.
verses.18: A man of little understanding gives a pledge hastily, and a guarantor for a friend is ensnared.
verses.19: One who loves transgression loves strife, and one who opens a door seeks destruction.
verses.20: A heart set on evil will not find good, and a twisted tongue will fall into trouble.
verses.21: A foolish child is a father's sorrow, and a foolish son brings no joy to his mother.
verses.22: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
verses.23: A bribe in the pocket of the wicked perverts the paths of justice.
verses.24: The eyes of a wise person are alert, while the eyes of a fool are at the farthest point of the earth.
verses.25: A foolish son is a father's anger, and a disgraceful daughter is a mother's sorrow.
verses.26: It is not good to punish the righteous, nor to strike nobles for doing right.
verses.27: One who holds his words in check knows wisdom. A man of great spirit is a person of understanding.
verses.28: Even a fool, when he is silent, is considered wise, and a man who seals his lips is deemed prudent.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The translation of "path" (מַלֵּהּ) as "peace in it" follows the metaphor of inner tranquility in contrast to external strife.
- v. 12: "Meeting a bear with claws" reflects the Hebrew idiom פָּגוֹשׁ דֹּב שַׁכּוּל, which literally means "meeting a bear in its den" — the danger of meeting a fool in his folly is likened to meeting a dangerous bear in its lair.
- v. 15: The translation of כִּי as "but" reflects the contrast between justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous.
- v. 16: The phrase "how much better it is than silver" is omitted as it is not in the Hebrew text; the text asks rhetorically why a fool would have money to buy wisdom.
- v. 24: The metaphor of "eyes of a fool are at the farthest point of the earth" is a literal rendering of עֵינֵי כְסִיל בִּקְצֵה־אָֽרֶץ, capturing the idea of a fool being oblivious or unaware.
